fields.label: Your story
fields.sample:
It all began on an ordinary Tuesday evening, in a small bookshop in Kadıköy. Two hands reaching for the same book at the same moment, a shy smile and the words “You take it, I’ll wait”… One of us ended up with the book, the other with a phone number.
Then came long walks, conversations that lasted until morning, cities we got lost in together. We became each other’s best friend; in laughter and in hard times alike, we were always on the same side.
One summer evening, a single question asked outside the bookshop where we first met changed everything. The answer was short: “Yes.” Now we want to write the most beautiful page of this story together with you.

elements.name: Haber metni
elements.text:
Seven years after they reached for the same book in a small book­shop in Kadıköy, the same two hands will wear the same ring. The couple de­cid­ed to marry after am­i­ca­bly set­tling their years-long debate over “who apol­o­gizes first.” Sources say the de­ci­sion came over a Sunday break­fast, right after an ar­gu­ment about whether the eggs should have onions or not.
The fam­i­lies, the first to hear the news, could not hold back tears of joy, while close friends issued a state­ment: “We knew it all along.” Word back­stage is that the bride’s mother drew up the henna night list just ten min­utes after hear­ing the news, while the groom’s father has al­ready begun mem­o­riz­ing his speech.
With wed­ding prepa­ra­tions in their final stages, the couple has just one re­quest: that you be there with them on the day. Guests are es­pe­cial­ly ad­vised to bring com­fort­able shoes, as the dance floor will stay open late. The full story, a behind-the-scenes look at the first meet­ing and an hour-by-hour pro­gram of the big day are on the inside pages.

elements.name: Tutanak metni
elements.text:
Groom: “You take it, I’ll wait.”
Bride: “No way, you reached first.”
Groom: “Then we’ll read it half and half.”
Bride: “The book, or life?”
Bookseller: “I’m closing the register; you two work it out.”

Bookseller (next day): “They brought the book back. Both of them. Hand in hand.”

Note: The book is still on the couple’s nightstand; they’re saving the last page to read together. The bookseller was the first person invited to the wedding.
